title: A new use case is decided, built from its records, held to the rules and merged proved
steps: On a fresh product repo, writes a use case with its requirement, flow and tests.
Writes the command it needs with its handler, and the files that build and test it.
Tries a write that breaks its aggregate's rules, which is refused with its reasons.
Records each test as automated with its file.
Checks the workspace.
Reads the use case requirement's Traceability.
Merges the branch's data into main.
expected_result: The wrong write left the data unchanged, the check finds no errors and no gaps for the use case, its requirement reads proved, and the merge keeps every record.

title: A product with code of its own is brought onto Lathe and checks clean with its outcomes and domains
steps: In a product repo with code, sets up Lathe and writes the first product record.
Writes two business outcomes and a domain with a capability serving them.
Writes a use case the code carries out and the command it needs, with the handler file that builds it.
Checks the workspace and reads its coverage.
expected_result: The check finds no errors, the outcomes and domain read back as written, and coverage shows the command built by the existing code.

title: A product written for the last Lathe moves to the new one and checks clean
steps: In a fresh product repo with data for the last Lathe, moves the product to the new Lathe.
Reads what it changed and what it left to do by hand, and does each by hand.
Checks the workspace.
expected_result: The move is one reviewable change and the check finds no errors on the new Lathe.

title: A change is seen in full before it is made, and moves only what the Owner chose
steps: In the desktop app on a one-domain product, opens a use case and reads what changing it would touch.
Asks Claude in the chat to change the use case.
Claude changes it through the product's commands and runs the check.
The Owner puts the turn's records under review and steps through each with its diff.
The Owner keeps the change.
expected_result: The records the turn changed are among those the reach named, the check finds no errors, and the review leaves the change in place.

title: A Reader given a part of a product they have not seen says why it exists and what proves it
steps: Opens the app on a product the Reader has not seen, given the name of one view.
Finds the view's record by its name.
Follows its links up to the requirement it fulfills and its use case.
Reads the business outcomes it serves.
Reads its Traceability and names the code files and the tests.
expected_result: The Reader names the requirement, use case and outcome behind the view, and the code and tests that build and prove it, in under five minutes.

title: The Owner reads a product's standing and names its weakest part
steps: On a product with one domain partly proved and one journey with a step carrying out nothing yet, checks the workspace.
Reads each domain's coverage.
Reads how far each journey is proved.
Reads the problems and what serves no outcome.
expected_result: The coverage, journey proof and problems name the unproved obligations, the unlinked step and the records that serve no outcome, each once.
